title: La inundación
goal: Help bail out a house after the rain and be fed for it
culture: When it rains hard the water comes into the houses down here, and helping bail is what a neighbour does rather than a kindness worth mentioning. Being fed for it is not optional: refusing the food is the insult, not the eating.

beats.objective: Ask whether the water got in
beats.good: Se metió el agua — the water got in. It is the sentence of the whole rainy season in this barrio.

beats.es: Toda la noche estuvo entrando. Desde las dos.
beats.good: Saying it back is doing something. She has been awake with a bucket since two and somebody noticing is not nothing.

beats.es: Agarre esa cubeta, vecino. Échele para afuera.
beats.objective: Get on with it, and say so
beats.en: Keep at it. I’ll give you a hand.
beats.good: Échele is go on, keep at it, throw it out. It is a verb of encouragement that means almost anything, and here it means both of you keep bailing.

beats.es: Ya, ya. Siéntese. Coma algo, aunque sea un poquito.
beats.objective: Accept — and turn it round on her
beats.good: She will feed you for helping and refusing is the insult. Telling her to eat too is the right answer, because she has not since it started.
